summary.text: Mark Spreitzer is a Democratic member of the Wisconsin State Senate who has represented District 15 since January 2023 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026, general election.
He previously served in the State Assembly from 2015 to 2023.

paragraphs.text: Mark Spreitzer lives in Beloit, Wisconsin, and earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Beloit College in 2009.
His professional experience includes working as an assistant director of alumni and parent relations and annual support at Beloit College and working for former U.S. Sen. Russ Feingold.
Spreitzer represented Assembly District 45 from 2015 to 2023 and took his Senate seat on January 3, 2023.

In a 2026 Ballotpedia survey, he said he had also served two terms on the Beloit City Council, chairs the Senate Democratic Caucus for 2025-2026 and the Legislative LGBTQ+ Caucus, and is the ranking Democratic member of the Committee on Government Operations, Labor, and Economic Development.

In the same survey, Spreitzer named housing, regulation of artificial intelligence and data centers, support for family farms, and reducing the burden of property taxes among his legislative priorities.
